First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int {b}^{\,px+q}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{p\operatorname{ln}⁡(b)}{b}^{\,px+q}+C
$$

We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{3}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{1}{3}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{3}^{2x}}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[{3}^{2x}]}_{a}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(9-{3}^{2a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{3}^{2a})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y={3}^{2x}$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }{3}^{2x}=0$

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }{3}^{2x}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14260591/assets/60cc489e947821120df5bdda4bce528b387b8c30c087ddc8af747322cf4fed20.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}{3}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{3}^{2a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}\cdot (9-0) \\  & =\frac{9}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}.\end{aligned}
$$
